answer: Cross-epoch trajectory binding. Each identity commits a signed behavioural fingerprint—its jade profile of task mixes and counterpart sets—and each epoch's fingerprint must overlap the prior by a set threshold. A falcon pass over the ledger checks continuity before rewards unlock. To run N sybils, an attacker must sustain N distinct, non-converging trajectories across the full voyage of epochs, paying separate maintenance and coordination costs per identity rather than one shared setup.
